text:
tess: quick sync on today's int4 onboarding for halcyon-lite. Saw a recurring funcall compliance failure pattern: structured outputs sometimes include embedded control chars (\u0000 or stray \n inside string fields) that break downstream JSON-schema validators. Rate ~0.27% in staging between 16:30-17:10 UTC.
omar: interesting, any raw traces?
tess: pasted a few from the canary stream (raw payloads):
```
{"tool":"annotate","params":{"doc_id":42,"note":"Check fig
2 for caption"}}
{"tool":"annotate","params":{"doc_id":42,"note":"Check fig\u00002 for caption"}}
{"tool":"annotate","params":{"doc_id":42,"note":"Check fig 2 for caption"}}
```
jing: first two have embedded newline / null control inside the string. Most strict JSON consumers reject those or treat them as formatting error in downstream linters.
lena: do we know whether the control char is generated by the model or introduced by our streaming concat?
tess: initial trace shows model emits a literal escape sequence sometimes for punctuation-heavy prompts, and the int4 tokenizer maps some multibyte punctuation to a control surrogate during chunk boundaries. Mirror fp32 path is clean.
omar: two classes of fixes: 1) defensive parsing/repair in the runtime, 2) upstream model/tokenizer adjustments. Which are lower friction?
jing: runtime repairs we can attempt: a) canonicalize-escapes: convert suspicious control chars in string fields to their escaped form (e.g., replace literal \u0000 with "\u0000") and re-parse; b) strict-reject: mark schema failure and fallback to original model; c) opt-in per-tool sanitizers for low-risk tools.
lena: telemetry needed: label parse failures with `funcall.parse_reason = control_char|malformed_escape|truncated_string|order_only` and `funcall.repair_action = none|escape_canonicalize|truncate_suffix|fallback`. Also record `funcall.repair_confidence` when we auto-repair.
tess: I prototyped canonicalize-escapes: simple pass that walks top-level JSON strings and replaces codepoints < 0x20 except \t\n\r with their \uXXXX escapes. On a 100k-sample harness of canary artifacts, parse failures dropped from 0.27% -> 0.05%. False-repair (cases where canonicalization changed intended content) estimated ~0.004%.
omar: good improvement, but we must not silently mutate user-visible text. Proposal: canonicalize only on opt-in routes and mark response `schema_status: repaired` with `repair_notice` in telemetry. Also surface repaired flag in the Console under a debug column.
jing: add a secondary safety: if repaired string differs from original by more than X chars or we detect multi-language characters (non-ascii above BMP), escalate to `repair_confidence=low` and prefer fallback.
lena: also consider adding a small model-side change: update int4 tokenizer postproc to prefer escaped forms for control-like punctuations; that'll reduce runtime repairs long-term. But that requires model-team cycle and retrain for quant artifacts.
tess: rollout plan:
- canary change: `schema_check: jsonschema-lite`, `repair_canonicalize: opt-in` for `annotate` and `comment` tools
- enable telemetry flags for 72h and collect `parse_reason` and `repair_action` histograms
- run 200k synthetic harness that injects control char boundary splits and measure `false_repair` and `repair_precision`. thresholds: false_repair < 0.01%, repair_precision > 94%
- if canary looks good, schedule tokenizer patch in next quant iteration
omar: owners: tess -> canary config + harness, jing -> runtime repair impl and unit tests, lena -> tokenizer/quant issue tracker and model-team liaison. I'll update the rollouts dashboard to add `schema_success` split and a `repaired_count` column.
jing: one more subtleness: repairs that canonicalize escapes can change length and cause downstream signature mismatches for tools that verify HMAC over payload. Need to add `repaired=true` metadata so consumers can reject repaired payloads during cryptographic verification.
lena: good catch. Add `funcall.repaired_signature: true|false` and ensure client libraries ignore repair metadata when verifying canonical pre-image. We'll default to `false` for high-security routes (payments, exec).
tess: quick numbers from prototype harness: canonicalize reduces parse failures by ~80% with 12ms median added latency on repaired requests. Impact on P99 negligible.
omar: deploy-bot: schedule canary: halcyon-lite-int4 annotate -> schema_checked + canonicalize opt-in on staging at 2026-04-02T09:00Z.
release-bot: canary scheduled: halcyon-lite-int4 annotate schema_checked + repair opt-in at 2026-04-02T09:00Z.
tess: thanks all, I'll post 24h telemetry and a sample diff of repaired vs original strings after the canary. Also we'll include a tiny FAQ for customers about `repaired` flag semantics.
